description: Phase 7: Refine the webview UIs (Device Manager, QR pairing, shared CSS) to match reference/adb-connect-cross-ide/ui-reference.png in both light and dark themes and at narrow widths, using only var(--vscode-*) theme variables. Verify by rendering the real media/*.css + media/*.js in a headless browser via the chrome-devtools/playwright MCP tools (NOT by reading CSS) and saving comparison screenshots under extensions/vscode/docs/ui/. Depends on FEAT-001 only for an orderly green base; UI work itself is independent of the test changes.
steps: Study reference/adb-connect-cross-ide/ui-reference.png: Device Manager = stacked cards (phone glyph, bold device name, mono ip:port line, right-aligned status pill Connected/Paired/Disconnected), a primary Reconnect + secondary Disconnect row, then a 3-tile action row (Pair New Device / Discover Devices / Settings); QR view = centered QR on a white quiet-zone, instruction text (Settings > Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair with QR code), and a highlighted hint such as 'Turn off Mobile data if enabled'. Minimal, native-IDE look.

Refine extensions/vscode/media/common.css, media/manager.css, media/qr.css to match the reference spacing, card treatment, pill placement and primary/secondary button hierarchy. Use only var(--vscode-*) variables (keep the existing --ac-* token mappings in common.css); the only hardcoded color allowed is the QR quiet-zone white in qr.css. Preserve the @media (max-width: 520px) narrow rules and the CSP/nonce shell (src/webview/html.ts).

Adjust DOM in media/manager.js and media/qr.js ONLY where the reference layout requires it (e.g. button ordering, hint line). Keep the {type:'state'} / {type:'qr'}+{type:'update'} message contracts and the window.AC h()/icon() helpers from media/icons.js intact.

Create a static harness that renders the real webview assets outside VS Code: extensions/vscode/docs/ui/harness.manager.html and harness.qr.html. Each stubs window.acquireVsCodeApi, defines a representative set of --vscode-* CSS variables for a DARK palette and (via a ?theme=light switch or a second file) a LIGHT palette, <link>s the real ../../media/common.css + manager.css|qr.css, loads ../../media/icons.js + manager.js|qr.js, then posts a representative state message (manager: a connected Pixel + paired Samsung + disconnected Nothing Phone; qr: a sample svg + waiting-for-scan then connected update).

Using the chrome-devtools MCP tools (load them via tool_load first; fall back to playwright MCP if needed), open each harness via file:// (or a tiny static server), set viewport, and capture screenshots: manager-dark.png, manager-light.png, manager-narrow.png (viewport width <=520px), qr-dark.png, qr-light.png. Save all under extensions/vscode/docs/ui/.

Visually compare each screenshot to ui-reference.png and iterate on the CSS until the Device Manager and QR views read as the same minimal native style in both palettes and at narrow width. Record the comparison outcome for VALIDATION.md (consumed by FEAT-003).
acceptance_criteria: extensions/vscode/docs/ui/ contains manager-dark.png, manager-light.png, manager-narrow.png, qr-dark.png, qr-light.png produced by an actual browser render (not hand-drawn), each visibly matching the layout/style of ui-reference.png.
media/common.css, manager.css, qr.css use var(--vscode-*) theme variables for all colors except the QR quiet-zone white; no new hardcoded palette colors.
The webview still uses the strict CSP/nonce shell and the {type:'state'}/{type:'qr'} message contracts (DOM contracts unchanged except deliberate layout tweaks).
npm run build still passes after CSS/JS edits.
verification: Browser screenshots under extensions/vscode/docs/ui/ exist and were generated by the chrome-devtools/playwright MCP tools against harness.manager.html and harness.qr.html (record the tool and steps in findings)
npm run -w extensions/vscode test:unit (confirms no regression from any shared-code edits)
findings:
DONE. Refined media/common.css, manager.css, qr.css to match reference/adb-connect-cross-ide/ui-reference.png in both palettes and at narrow width, using only var(--vscode-*) variables (QR quiet-zone #fff is the only hardcoded color; kept the --ac-* token mappings). No DOM edits to manager.js/qr.js were needed: the manager DOM already produced the reference's stacked-card layout (phone glyph, bold name, mono ip:port, right-aligned status pill, primary Reconnect + secondary action row, tile action grid), and the one real QR-layout defect was pure CSS — qr.css centered a <main> element that qr.js never renders (it renders into #app), so the QR view was left-aligned; changed the selector to #app so the QR, instructions and buttons now center on the white quiet-zone as in the reference. Also: bumped device-card padding/row-gap and name size for the native spacing, and gave .pill.plain a subtle var(--vscode-badge-background) chip so the colored status pill stands out. Preserved @media (max-width:520px) narrow rules and the CSP/nonce shell (src/webview/html.ts) and the {type:'state'}/{type:'qr'}+{type:'update'} message contracts.

SCREENSHOT METHOD: Built static harnesses extensions/vscode/docs/ui/harness.manager.html and harness.qr.html. Each stubs window.acquireVsCodeApi, injects a representative DARK/LIGHT --vscode-* palette (?theme=light|dark), <link>s the REAL ../../media/common.css + manager.css|qr.css, loads the REAL ../../media/icons.js + manager.js|qr.js, then posts a representative message (manager: connected Pixel 9 Pro + paired Samsung S24 + disconnected Nothing Phone (2); qr: a demo pairing SVG + waiting-for-scan update). chrome-devtools MCP (loaded via tool_load) could render but its screenshot writer is sandboxed to a root outside this repo, so screenshots were captured with the playwright MCP tools (browser_navigate/browser_resize/browser_take_screenshot) against a local static server (python3 -m http.server 8777 serving extensions/vscode; playwright blocks file://). Saved to the playwright temp root then copied into extensions/vscode/docs/ui/. Viewports: manager 820x900 (dark, light), manager 500px-wide (narrow, <=520px triggers the stacked media query), qr 820x820 (dark, light).

FILES PRODUCED: extensions/vscode/docs/ui/{manager-dark.png, manager-light.png, manager-narrow.png, qr-dark.png, qr-light.png} — all real browser renders of the actual webview assets.

COMPARISON OUTCOME (consumed by FEAT-003 VALIDATION.md): both views read as the same minimal native-IDE style as ui-reference.png. Device Manager — stacked cards, left phone glyph, bold device name, mono ip:port meta, right-aligned status pill (Connected=green fill / Available / Disconnected), primary Reconnect + secondary icon-action row, and the Pair/Discover/Settings tile grid; identical in dark and light; at 500px the badges and actions wrap onto their own rows and the tile grid reflows cleanly. QR — centered QR on a white quiet-zone, the 'Settings > Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with QR code' instruction, a 'Waiting for scan' status with countdown, Cancel + 'Use six-digit pairing code instead', and a 'Having trouble?' hints disclosure; matches in both palettes. VERIFICATION: npm run build PASS; npm run -w extensions/vscode test:unit PASS (4 tests, no regression).
